stories.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania
stories.summary: The drone, which is believed to have entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus, was shot down by an Italian fighter jet in between the cities of Vilnius and Kaunas. There have been no reports of casualties or damage.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MbDj Lithuanian authorities published images of what they said were the charred remains of the drone Image: Lithuanian Army/Handout/REUTERS Advertisement A drone which entered Lithuanian airspace in the early hours of Tuesday morning was shot down by NATO fighter jets in between the cities of Vilnius and Kaunas, Lithuanian authorities have confirmed. Lithuania 's National Crisis Management Center (NKVC) said the drone most likely came from neighboring Belarus , an ally of Russia in its ongoing war against Ukraine , and was flying west when it was shot down by an Italian jet. Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda thanked the military alliance for its "swift response." "With Russia intensifying its aggression against Ukraine , such readiness is vital for our region," he wrote on social media. "Together with our NATO Allies, Lithuania will defend its airspace." Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said the NATO response sent "a clear message that NATO stands vigilant, committed, and ready."
